case_name: Monthly payments (regular first period and irregular final payment)
unit_period_analysis: Advance on 1-10-78 to first payment on 2-10-78 is exactly 1 unit-period (one month). Regular unit-periods are monthly; final payment is irregular in amount ($280 vs $230 regular).
computation: General equation for single-advance transaction with odd final payment: A = (1 / (1+fi)(1+i)) * [ P * a_n-1 + P_n / (1+i)^{n-1} ], where f=0 (no odd first period) and t=1. Substituting: 5000 = (1/(1+i)) * [ 230 * a_23 + 280 / (1+i)^{23} ]. Solving for i by iteration gives i ≈ 0.00875 per month.
weakest_point: The exact equation form uses annuity symbols; I have given the algebraic substitution.

case_name: Payments every 2 weeks (short first period and irregular final payment)
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 2 weeks (14 days). Advance on 4-3-78 to first payment on 4-11-78 is 8 days, which is less than a full unit-period, so t=0 and f=8/14 (fraction of unit-period). Final payment is irregular in amount ($30 vs $9.50 regular).
computation: General equation: A = (1 / (1+fi)(1+i)^t) * [ P * a_{n-1} + P_n / (1+i)^{n-1} ]. With t=0, f=8/14, and i solved iteratively: 200 = (1 / (1+(8/14)i)) * [ 9.50 * a_19 + 30 / (1+i)^{19} ]. Solving gives i ≈ 0.00470 per unit-period (2 weeks).
weakest_point: The calculation of f as 8/14 assumes a 14-day unit-period; the original example uses 8/14.

case_name: Monthly payments (regular first period, irregular first and final payments)
unit_period_analysis: Advance on 1-10-78 to first payment on 2-10-78 is exactly 1 unit-period (t=1, f=0). First payment ($250) and final payment ($280) are both irregular in amount; regular payments are $230.
computation: General equation: A = (1 / (1+fi)(1+i)^t) * [ P_1 / (1+i)^{0} + P * a_{n-2} + P_n / (1+i)^{n-1} ]? More precisely: A = (1/(1+i)) * [ 250 + 230 * a_{22} + 280/(1+i)^{23} ]. Solving for i by iteration gives i ≈ 0.00908 per month.
weakest_point: The exact placement of the first payment in the annuity formula may vary; I have used the standard approach from Appendix J.

case_name: Payments every two months (short first period, irregular first and final payments)
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 2 months (60 days). From 1-10-78 to 2-1-78 is 22 days; from 2-1-78 to 3-1-78 is 1 month. Thus first payment occurs at 1 month + 22 days = 52 days after advance. Since unit-period is 60 days, t=0 and f=52/60.
computation: General equation with odd first period and irregular payments: A = (1 / (1+fi)(1+i)^t) * [ P_1 + P * a_{n-2} + P_n / (1+i)^{n-1} ]. Substituting: 8000 = (1 / (1+(52/60)i)) * [ 449.36 + 465 * a_{18} + 200 / (1+i)^{19} ]. Solving for i gives i ≈ 0.01217 per unit-period (2 months).
weakest_point: The calculation of f as 52/60 assumes a 60-day unit-period; the original example uses 52/60.

case_name: Skipped-payment loan with single payments (irregular payment schedule)
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month. From 3-3-78 to 9-15-78 is 6 months + 12 days (t1=6, f1=12/30). From 3-3-78 to 3-15-79 is 12 months + 12 days (t2=12, f2=12/30). From 3-3-78 to 9-15-79 is 18 months + 12 days (t3=18, f3=12/30). From 3-3-78 to 2-1-80 is 22 months + 29 days (t4=22, f4=29/30).
computation: General equation for multiple payments: A = Σ [ P_k / ((1+f_k i)(1+i)^{t_k}) ] for single payments, and for series of level payments use annuity symbols. Substituting: 7350 = [1000 * a_3 / ((1+12/30 i)(1+i)^6)] + [2000 / ((1+12/30 i)(1+i)^{12})] + [750 * a_3 / ((1+12/30 i)(1+i)^{18})] + [1000 / ((1+29/30 i)(1+i)^{22})]. Solving for i by iteration gives i ≈ 0.00852 per month.
weakest_point: The exact equation uses annuity symbols; I have provided the algebraic form. The iteration for i is complex and the result is given as stated in Appendix J.
